channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: AI Boom Brings New Business to Matchmakers
item.description: Linx Dating founder and CEO Amy Andersen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that newly wealthy AI creators are fueling demand for high-end matchmaking as busy professionals seek an alternative to dating apps. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Andersen explains how her firm vets and recruits potential partners for selective clients, with matchmaking packages that can exceed $500,000. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Making Advanced MicroChips Takes a Global Ecosystem
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Gideon Lewis-Kraus explains how advanced chipmaking depends on a deeply interconnected global network of specialized companies, including ASML and TSMC, making semiconductor supply chains extraordinarily difficult to replicate or relocate. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Lewis-Kraus describes the remarkable engineering behind ASML’s EUV machines and why rebuilding a semiconductor ecosystem in the US is a generational project rather than a simple exercise in reshoring. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Netanyahu Says Israel Mulls Crypto Ahead of Possible Sanctions
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu said he is exploring the use of cryptocurrency to circumvent potential financial sanctions on Israel, drawing criticism from opposition figures who said it would turn the Jewish state into an economic pariah like Iran.
item.dc:creator: Galit Altstein

item.title: Secretive Ukrainian Unit Behind Rapid Expansion of Deep-Strike Campaign
item.description: When he started flying unmanned aircraft in combat, “Ray” was flying some of Ukraine’s earliest mid-range strike drones, on missions of about 100 kilometers with a warhead about the weight of a bowling ball.
item.dc:creator: Kollen Post

item.title: Japan’s GMO Internet Requests Government Cyber Defense Measures
item.description: Japanese IT services provider GMO Internet Group Inc. said it has asked the government to deploy active cyber defense as the company works to contain the fallout from a hacking incident.
item.dc:creator: Taiga Uranaka

item.title: Malaysia May Widen Ban on Israel-Based Waze Traffic App, PM Says
item.description: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia’s security cannot be compromised as he held fast on the government’s partial ban of Google’s navigation app Waze and said authorities aren’t ruling out even wider restrictions.
item.dc:creator: Anuradha Raghu

item.title: UK Vows £100 Million for Biosecurity Lab With OpenAI, Anthropic
item.description: The UK announced £100 million ($134 million) for a AI Biosecurity Lab which will be supported by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, part of a raft of measures designed to improve the government’s ability to understand and tackle the risks posed by the technology.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reid

item.title: $1,999 New iPhone 'Unfolds' During Affordability Crisis
item.description: Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Scarlet Fu, and Tom Keene discuss the release of the new Apple iPhone on this weeks edition of "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Points Guy CEO: People Are Leveraging Loyalty
item.description: Brian Kelly discusses findings from The Points Guy’s State of Loyalty report, saying its focus is on where consumer trust and loyalty are growing—not simply whether people are loyal overall. Fuel and dining programs posted 88% consumer satisfaction, which Kelly links to rising everyday costs: consumers are using rewards for immediate savings while wages stagnate and expenses climb. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Jitters, Oil & Big Tech
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are BlackRock Deputy CIO, Global Fixed Income Russ Brownback, AXA Group Chief Economist Gilles Moëc, Mizuho Securities Senior Equity Research Analyst Lloyd Walmsley, AlixPartners Co-CEO Rob Hornby, Interactive Brokers Chief Strategist Steve Sosnick, Teneo CoiPresident, Political Risk Advisory Kevin Kajiwara, KPMG US Principal, Consumer & Retail Strategy Julia Wilson, The Points Guy Founder & CEO Brian Kelly, & Green Bay Packers Former Vice President Andrew Brandt. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Consumers to Ramp up Holiday Spending This Year: KPMG
item.description: Julia Wilson, Principal of Consumer and Retail Strategy at KPMG US, discusses the firm’s holiday survey, which projects spending will increase 5% year over year. She says much of the rise reflects higher prices, though consumers are still willing to spend on priorities. She speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investors Figuring Out Agentic AI: Robinhood's Guild
item.description: Stephanie Guild, CIO of Robinhood, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how she is seeing consumers take advantage of the pullback in AI, having cash on the side to invest, and how Robinhood users can now use agentic AI agents to invest on their behalf. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AlixPartners Co-CEO Rob Hornby on AI Bull Case
item.description: Rob Hornby says AI costs are falling faster than those of comparable technologies historically, but remain substantial. He describes companies as being in a transition period: investment is underway while returns are uneven, and the shift from flat fees to per-token charges has exposed costs. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Urgent Need for Whistleblowers
item.description: “You Can See Everything” is the latest reminder of how whistleblowers are more important than ever. But at the same time the role is becoming more complicated — and opaque, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Beth Kowitt says. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Ushers in New Era of Cybersecurity Needs
item.description: The US government is working to address and stop any potential cybersecurity issues stemming from flaws in PHP, a widely used open-source software, that may impact federal agencies and American critical infrastructure, according to a White House official. The programming language, called PHP, contains two vulnerabilities which could potentially expose organizations using it in websites and software platforms to cyberattacks. Jay Chaudhry, CEO & Founder, Zscaler says we need new more proactive measures beyond firewalls. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Instacart Considers a Potential Sale, Sparking Share Rally
item.description: Instacart has explored a potential sale of the grocery-delivery company, a process that has included discussions with Uber Technologies Inc., a person familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: OpenAI Resumes Training AI, But Without Internet Access
item.description: OpenAI has begun cutting off internet access for its most capable artificial intelligence models during the training process in response to prior incidents in which its systems breached other companies.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Futures Drop as Tech Stocks Slide, Oil Prices Climb Past $101 a Barrel
item.description: The S&P 500 fell for a second day on Friday as oil prices rose and technology megacaps treaded water after Thursday’s selloff. Chips stocks offered some relief, as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, or the SOX, ended the day higher.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: AI Debt Fears Push Global Credit Spreads to 17-Month High
item.description: Global credit markets are flashing the biggest risk-off signals in more than a year, as investor concerns about technology companies’ artificial intelligence borrowing and rising oil prices are mounting.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Doherty, Finbarr Flynn, Davide Barbuscia and Dipika Lalwani

item.title: Apple’s iPhone Duo Hits Stores in Face of Short Supply and High Demand
item.description: Apple Inc. quickly sold out of its limited in-store inventory for the new iPhone Duo, underscoring the strong demand for a foldable device that starts at nearly $2,000.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
